title: Junior Prodigy & Kids Accelerated Pathway
subtitle: A fun chess adventure made just for kids! 🎉
description: A giant, colorful chess adventure built for kids! Easy words, silly names for every move, fun games instead of boring drills, and gold stars every step of the way. No hard chess words — everything is explained like a friend would explain it.

phases.name: 🐣 Quest 1: Meet Your Chess Team! (Months 1–2)
phases.focus: Learn what each piece is and how it moves — like meeting new friends! We play the "Pawn Race", the "Knight Jump Maze", and "Bishop Laser Beam" games so every rule turns into a game, not homework.
outcomes: Know every piece and its move by heart
Set up the board all by yourself
Never touch a piece by accident — good chess manners!

phases.name: 🏰 Quest 2: The Kingdom & Its Secrets (Months 3–4)
phases.focus: Discover the board's hidden map (easy square names), plus 3 magic moves every chess wizard knows: Castling, En Passant, and Pawn Promotion — explained with simple pictures and stories.
outcomes: Find any square on the board in 3 seconds
Use castling to keep your King safe
Turn a pawn into a Queen like magic

phases.name: ⚡ Quest 3: Tactical Superpowers! (Months 5–7)
phases.focus: Meet the "Fork Monster", the "Unbreakable Pin", and the "Laser Skewer" — our fun nicknames for real chess tactics. One tiny 5-minute puzzle a day builds superhero pattern-spotting skills.
outcomes: Spot a Fork or Pin in under 3 seconds
Solve 500+ kid-friendly puzzles
Say "Checkmate!" with confidence

phases.name: 👑 Quest 4: Checkmate Detective (Months 8–9)
phases.focus: Become a checkmate detective! Learn the simplest ways to win the game (King + Queen, King + Rook) using easy step-by-step pictures, no memorizing needed.
outcomes: Deliver checkmate with a Queen or Rook every time
Never accidentally cause a boring draw (stalemate)

phases.name: 🧭 Quest 5: Little Strategist (Months 10–11)
phases.focus: Learn to make a simple plan instead of just reacting — like a chess superhero with a game plan! Includes the "Superhero Pawn Race" and easy opening ideas (control the middle first).
outcomes: Make a simple plan before moving
Control the center squares from move one

phases.name: 🏆 Quest 6: First Tournament Hero! (Month 12)
phases.focus: Get ready for a real tournament! Learn chess clock manners, how to write down moves, shaking hands after the game, and — most important — being a good sport whether you win or lose.
outcomes: Play in a real first tournament
Win or lose with a smile and a handshake
Earn an official Junior Chess Rating

rewards: 🏅 A shiny badge for every superpower learned
🎓 A "Junior Champion" certificate at the end
parentNote: Parents & coaches: every lesson uses short sentences, big friendly pictures, and celebrates effort over results. No pressure, just progress — one gold star at a time.

title: 3-Year Club Player Mastery
subtitle: From Complete Beginner to Strong Club Player (1800–2000 Elo)
description: A comprehensive, month-by-month journey through fundamentals, tactical motifs, positional strategy, endgames, calculation discipline, and tournament psychology.

phases.name: Year 1: Foundation & Tactical Vision
phases.focus: Rules, piece values, coordinate fluency, basic checkmates (K+Q, K+R, 2R), forks, pins, skewers, discovered attacks, double attacks, and pawn endings.
outcomes: Solve mate-in-1 and mate-in-2 instantly
Spot 1-2 move tactical shots
Reach 1200+ online rating

phases.name: Year 2: Positional Understanding & Intermediate Strategy
phases.focus: Pawn structures (isolated, doubled, passed, chains), open files & outposts, bishop pair dynamics, rook endgames (Lucena & Philidor), prophylaxis, and opening repertoires.
outcomes: Formulate structured middlegame plans
Execute rook endgame drawing and winning techniques
Reach 1500+ Elo

phases.name: Year 3: Advanced Calculation & Tournament Play
phases.focus: Deep candidate move calculation, candidate pruning, visualization without moving pieces, time management, psychological toughness, and engine-assisted post-game analysis.
outcomes: Calculate 4–6 plies deep with blunder checking
Compete successfully in rated OTB tournaments
Attain 1800–2000 Elo

title: Master Class & Titled Player Pathway
subtitle: 1800 → 2200+ (Candidate Master, FIDE Master & Master Norms)
description: An elite training curriculum designed for players seeking CM, FM, and IM titles. Delves into deep master prophylaxis, complex pawn structures, calculation trees, and engine prep.

phases.name: Module 1: Advanced Calculation & Candidate Pruning
phases.focus: Kotov trees, Dvoretsky candidate selection methods, visualizing complex pawn endgames 8 plies deep, dynamic sacrifices, and defense under acute time pressure.
outcomes: Spot quiet forcing moves in chaotic complications
Eliminate calculation blind spots

phases.name: Module 2: Master Pawn Formations & Structure Blueprint
phases.focus: Deep exploration of classic pawn structures: The Carlsbad Formation (minority attack vs central clamp), The Hedgehog (b6/d6/e6/a6 dynamics), Maróczy Bind, Isolani (d4 pawn dynamics), and Hanging Pawns.
outcomes: Understand deep positional plans without memorizing opening moves
Execute strategic piece regroupings

phases.name: Module 3: Prophylaxis & Karpovian Positional Squeeze
phases.focus: Nimzowitsch prophylaxis, Petrosian and Karpov space constriction techniques, restriction of opponent counterplay, and piece color-complex domination.
outcomes: Smother opponent plans before they materialize
Win games on subtle positional superiority

phases.name: Module 4: Complex Endgames & Practical Conversion
phases.focus: Vancura defense in rook endings, Queen vs Rook theoretical conversion, opposite-colored bishop fortress breaking, knight vs bishop imbalance mastery, and tablebase nuances.
outcomes: Hold drawing resources in 4v3 rook endings
Flawlessly convert technical advantages

phases.name: Module 5: Modern Opening Repertoire & Engine Preparation
phases.focus: Building a bulletproof opening file with Stockfish/Leela, novelties at move 15–20, target-specific opponent scouting, and opening transition to favorite middlegames.
outcomes: Possess a complete FIDE-ready opening repertoire with Black and White

phases.name: Module 6: Psychological Matchplay & Title Norm Strategy
phases.focus: Tournament fatigue management, swiss tournament pairing tactics, playing for a win with Black, crisis management, and psychological resilience.
outcomes: Score title norms (CM/FM) in rated FIDE round-robin & open events

title: Grandmaster Opening Repertoire Blueprint
subtitle: World-Class Opening Systems for White & Black with Deep Ideas
description: Stop memorizing arbitrary move lists. Learn the ideas, piece setups, key pawn breaks, and tactical traps behind every major master opening system.

phases.name: White Repertoire: Dynamic 1.e4 (The Attacker’s Arsenal)
phases.focus: Italian Game (Giuoco Pianissimo & Evans Gambit), Ruy Lopez (Anti-Marshall systems), Open Sicilian mainlines (English Attack vs Najdorf, Yugoslav vs Dragon), and French/Caro-Kann advanced structures.
outcomes: Claim early initiative in every 1.e4 game
Understand typical attacking sacrifices on e6/f7/h7

phases.name: White Repertoire: Solid & Squeezing 1.d4 / 1.c4 (Positional Mastery)
phases.focus: Queen’s Gambit Declined & Slav Exchange, Catalan Opening (g3 bishop power), King’s Indian Defense Classical Mar del Plata lines, and English Opening setups.
outcomes: Dominate long-term pawn structures and space advantages

phases.name: Black Repertoire vs 1.e4: The Sicilian Counterstrike & Classical 1...e5
phases.focus: The Sicilian Classical / Scheveningen complex, plus solid Open Game 1...e5 (Petrov & Two Knights Defense) for rock-solid stability.
outcomes: Neutralize White’s first-move advantage and counter-attack on queenside

phases.name: Black Repertoire vs 1.d4: Nimzo-Indian & King’s Indian Dynamic Play
phases.focus: Nimzo-Indian Defense (4.Qc2 & 4.e3), paired with the Queen’s Indian / Bogo-Indian, and the King’s Indian Defense king-hunt pawn storms.
outcomes: Active piece play and winning chances with Black against 1.d4

title: Rapid Calculation & Blitz Pattern Arena
subtitle: High-Speed Tactical Reflexes, Puzzle Rush & Blindfold Drills
description: Train your brain to spot tactical patterns in sub-second intervals. Features Woodpecker Method repeat cycles, blindfold visualization stages, and time-pressure calculation puzzles.

phases.name: Phase 1: Sub-Second Motif Recognition (Level 1–3)
phases.focus: 1,000 foundational mate-in-1, fork, pin, skewer, and discovered attack positions drilled until identification is subconscious.
outcomes: Under 2-second tactical recognition
Elimination of one-move blunders

phases.name: Phase 2: The Woodpecker Cycling Protocol
phases.focus: 500 intermediate puzzle sets solved across 7 progressive time cycles (Cycle 1: 4 weeks, Cycle 2: 2 weeks, Cycle 7: 24 hours).
outcomes: Imprint master tactical motifs into long-term photographic memory

phases.name: Phase 3: Blindfold Board Visualization
phases.focus: Square color guessing, diagonal intersections, knight route calculation without board, and blindfold mini-game reconstruction.
outcomes: Calculate lines 5 plies deep completely in your mind’s eye
